subject: BrightHealth pilot: weekly fleet decision digest
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightHealth pilot: weekly fleet decision digest

Team —

Quick recap + concrete asks ahead of the weekly fleet planning call (Wed 11am PT). BrightHealth expects to finalize pilot terms by mid-Oct; they signaled a target pilot start in Jan 2027 that looks like:

- Expected steady-state inference: ~1.2M prompt tokens/day (chat + embeddings mix)
- Peak concurrency window: 6–8k concurrent requests (short chat turns)
- Quality SLA: p95 latency <= 400ms for chat paths

From our sizing model (attached) this maps to an approximate reserved need of 18–24 A100-equivalent GPUs depending on batching/quantization tradeoffs. The ask from sales is to present a firm recommendation at tomorrow’s call on:

1) Reserve commit recommended (conservative vs. optimistic) — pick a single number to propose to customer.
2) Canary plan: how many dedicated slots to reserve for canary + fallback multi-tenant route.
3) Short-term burst/capacity backstop and cost delta for finance.

Please review the attached BrightHealth_Pilot_capacity_model_v2.xlsx and the allocation matrix (allocation_matrix_v3.pdf). Specific requests:

- Laura: validate the 18–24 GPU equivalence given current kernel/sequence estimates and whether model quantization (int8) could safely reduce to 14–16.
- Ben: provide estimated monthly $ commit delta for 18 vs 24 GPUs (include burst credits and SLO penalty runway).
- Mina: confirm infra lead times for reserving 20 GPUs in us-west region and whether we can stagger provisioning (10 + 10) to reduce immediate capital.

I’ll be on the call with Alex Brown from BrightHealth to run through the mutual action plan. If we can land a recommended commit and a 2-week canary plan, sales can push for signature this month.

Thanks —
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

Attachments: BrightHealth_Pilot_capacity_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), allocation_matrix_v3.pdf (PDF)

On Tue, 29 Sep 2026 at 09:12, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
>
> Quick recap + concrete asks ahead of the weekly fleet planning call (Wed 11am PT).

Thanks, Aditya — read the model. High level notes:

- With our current runtime kernels and expected sequence length distribution (median 64 tokens, 95% <= 320), the conservative path (no quantization) lands at ~22 A100-equivalent GPUs to comfortably hit p95 <= 400ms with continuous batching.
- If BrightHealth is comfortable with int8 quantization + a prioritized KV-caching plan (hot prefixes cached), we can credibly target ~15–17 GPUs without breaking latency SLOs. That assumes we accept a small increase in tail variance for cold prefixes.
- Canary plan: recommend reserving 6 dedicated GPUs for a 2-week canary (feed real traffic, verify e2e telemetry). Keep a multi-tenant fallback pool sized to handle 30% of expected peak if canary shows issues.

Open question for infra: can we provision 6 GPUs within 7 business days for the canary and then scale to 20 over 30 days? If yes, staggered provisioning is reasonable.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Platform Capacity
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightHealth pilot: weekly fleet decision digest

Aditya / all —

Numbers attached in a simple breakdown (see BrightHealth_Pilot_capacity_model_v2.xlsx, tab "commit_cost"). Quick summary: monthly committed cost estimates (US-West pricing band):

- 18 GPUs reserved (baseline config): $162k / month commitment
- 22 GPUs reserved (middle): $198k / month commitment
- 24 GPUs reserved (conservative): $216k / month commitment

Burst credits (on top of commit): recommend offering 20% burst pool for first 3 months while they ramp — incremental expected spend if used ~ $8–$12k/month.

Risk/cushion guidance: If we present 20 GPUs as the recommended commit (balancing runway + cost), we can price the pilot with a 6-month minimum, include 10% discounted burst, and provide an SLA band (p95 latency target) with graduated credits for violations.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal FinOps Analyst
Redwood Inference

Attachment references: BrightHealth_Pilot_capacity_model_v2.xlsx (commit_cost tab)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, alex.brown@brighthealth.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightHealth pilot: weekly fleet decision digest

Thanks for the fast turnaround —

Summary + what we’ll present to BrightHealth at today’s 11am PT:

- Recommended commit: 20 GPUs (us-west) as a balanced recommendation. Rationale: mid-point between Laura's conservative runtime sizing and quantized optimistic scenario; allows staging to 20 with canary safety margin.
- Canary plan: 6 GPUs for two weeks (dedicated); multi-tenant fallback sized at ~30% peak for cold starts.
- Commercial ask: 6-month pilot minimum at $195k/month commit with 20% burst credits for month 1–3; included SLA targets with tiered credits. (Ben will finalize the exact numbers in the offer sheet.)
- Infra ask: ability to provision 6 GPUs within 7 business days and scale to 20 within 30 days. Mina — please confirm ETA and any blockers.

Alex — I’ll walk through the mutual action plan and allocation matrix when we meet at 11. If we can get verbal buy-in on commit sizing + canary timeline, we’ll share a DocuSign pilot addendum by Friday.

-- 
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
